candidate_nonpassing_gates.reason: Release requires terminal unittest OK on stderr, nonzero tests and zero skips

findings: The e0 candidate, standalone and integrated full unittest runs each executed 4335 tests and recorded the same three SameCoreBuildInputTests ELF-linker-driver spelling errors. Candidate and standalone additionally recorded two skips. The earlier separate six-outcome timeout is not the failure shown in these full-release original logs.

The b121 candidate and standalone full unittest processes returned zero with 4335 tests and OK (skipped=2). Strict zero-skip qualification therefore correctly failed. The candidate verbose original names both ConvergedNativeGraphTests methods; the standalone quiet original reports only the skip count and does not name methods.

The b121 integrated original full unittest run executed 4335 tests with no failure, error or skip, and all eight integrated gates passed. Its actual environment records both CLANG and HEPTA_CLANG as /usr/lib/llvm-20/bin/clang.

The exact b121 workflow exports CLANG but not HEPTA_CLANG in its selected verification tool step. The exact standalone qualifier likewise configures CLANG but not HEPTA_CLANG. The two candidate skipped methods require HEPTA_CLANG in their unchanged decorator. This is an environment provisioning inconsistency; no new production execution error is present in the b121 selected unit records.

Minimum proposed repair: synchronize HEPTA_CLANG to the same explicitly selected compiler in the workflow and standalone environment, preserving existing teardown, no-skip rules, test decorators and admissions. A repair requires its own source-bound actual execution; these original failed workflows are never reclassified.
